MAJOR: Canonical edge set (SEED) is enforced only for `tenant_id` tenancy edges derived from schema; non-tenancy canonical edges (e.g. `artifacts.runs.run_id`, `runs.projects.project_id`, `stages/attempts` chain) are silently droppable — `check()` will still pass, so the "relationships recorded" guarantee is only partially enforced.

SEED list is hardcoded duplicate truth living in two places (script + registry JSON) with no consistency check; the `canonical: true` flag written to the registry is never read or validated by the tool — drift between the two copies is undetectable.

Status transitions are self-attesting: `planned → exists` flips based solely on the owner backlog item being in `DONE`, not on verified delivery (object-store "exists" is validated only against a hardcoded `OBJECT_META = {"artifacts","stored_objects"}` set, not actual bucket/backend state). A falsely-closed item silently upgrades store status and `migration_status` to "migrated".

Rationale/provenance loss: `reason: "global authored config -> file (git-reviewed)"` on ~40 retained file targets replaced with empty-string `ref`/`owner_item`; the gate accepts empty strings, so the "planned targets name the owning EDP item" invariant degenerates into a shape check with no information content.
MINOR: `REQUIRED_TRIGGERS` is a hardcoded tuple in tooling; trigger drift (rename/split in migrations) will break the fast gate with no config-level override — consider deriving from migrations or a config artifact.
`--verbose` is parsed and passed to `_report` but ignored there (all problems always print); dead parameter.

`_expected_status` special-cases `kind == "table" and backend == "file"` and `retained_reason` presence to yield "retained", mixing "where data lives" with "why it wasn't migrated" — semantics are subtle and easy to misapply on future stores.

Self-test covers only 3 scenarios; it does not exercise the object-store "exists" validation, the required-trigger check, or the non-tenancy canonical-edge removal case (which, per MAJOR #1, would pass — a test gap that masks the enforcement gap).
`kind ∈ {file,view,derived}` accepts `backend ∈ {file,derived}` — a `view` backed by `file` passes silently; looseness in an otherwise strict gate.

`check()` re-derives expectations from `target.status` rather than an independent source, so a store whose target status is wrong-but-internally-consistent passes; consider an independent existence oracle per backend.
NIT: `glob` import used for `_sql_files`; `Path.glob` would be more idiomatic and testable.

`_statements_after` quote/paren scanning is hand-rolled; acceptable for tooling but fragile if migrations ever embed dollar-quoted bodies (`$$ ... $$`) — a `DO $$` block would break column extraction.
`retained_reason` is stuffed inside `target` alongside `reason`; two similarly-named fields coexist in the same object — naming collision risk for future readers.
SUMMARY: Solid incremental slice: new relationship gate wired consistently into both `precheck.py` and `ci-cd-gates.json`, fail-closed checks, and a self-test with negative scenarios — directionally right. Top risks: (1) canonical relationship enforcement is only partial (tenancy edges only), so the SEED/registry duplication is undetectable drift; (2) status flips driven by backlog-item state rather than verified delivery weaken the integrity of `migration_status`; (3) blanket replacement of `reason` with empty `ref`/`owner_item` on retained file targets discards provenance while satisfying the gate shape. Recommend tightening enforcement to the full canonical set, validating the seed against the registry, and preserving rationale text before merge.
